To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) TAT from liver and kidney is inactivated by the membraneous fraction from liver and kidney, (2) ATP protects TAT from the membraneous inactivation in vitro, (3) ATP is not the only nucleotide that is effective, (4) ATP causes reactivation of TAT in the presence of membraneous fractions from rat liver.
a membrane bound enzyme from rat liver inactivates and ATP-dependently reactivates tyrosine aminaotransferase.

In summary, our research is concerned with
a membrane bound system which may be of physiological significance for the regulation of gluconeogenesis.
a possible mechanism of the short term control of gluconeogenic enzymes.
a membrane bound system in the cell which is able to inactivate glucogenic enzymes and to stabilize them in an ATP-dependent fashion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the membrane bound system is a general regulatory mechanism in control of gluco-neogenesis.
a membrane bound enzyme complex in liver and kidney is involved in the control of gluconeogenic enzymes by hormones via cyclic AMP and cyclic GMP as second messengers.

the membrane bound enzymes from liver and kidney are responsible for the regulation of the activity of the enzymes of gluconeogenesis and of the enzymes which are involved in the control of gluconeogenic flux.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the membrane bound enzymes from liver and kidney are capable to inactivate TAT, and that this inactivation can be fully protected by ATP in the presence of liver membrane bound enzymes, but only partially in the presence of kidney membrane bound enzymes.
inactivation and stabilization of TAT in the presence of membrane bound enzymes from liver are controlled by ATP, cyclic AMP, and GMP.
the membrane bound enzyme system in kidney and liver may represent the common regulatory attack of the short term acting hormones at the gluconeogenic enzymes in the two organs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the membrane bound system is a general regulatory mechanism for the control of gluconeogenic enzymes.
a membrane bound enzyme inactivating TAT in vitro is present in the liver as well as in the kidney cortex.
the membrane bound system is not specific for PEP carboxykinases but may be involved in a general control of gluconeogenic enzyme systems.
